status: Authored synthetic benchmark; held-out Monte Carlo seeds not yet executed by reviewer
cost_units: Abstract measurement cost, not wall time or money
likelihood_orientation: Each row is a hidden hypothesis; each column is an observable outcome
noise_contract: Observations conditionally independent given hypothesis, action and repetition; repeated actions allowed
candidate: After every observation update Bayes posterior, choose affordable action maximizing expected posterior entropy decrease in bits divided by action cost
terminal_decision: MAP hypothesis, ties by hypothesis order
stop: Exactly exhaust budget; do not use a confidence-dependent stopping rule

baselines.best_fixed: Full diagnostic once; strongest fixed schedule by exact expected terminal accuracy among all affordable precommitted schedules
baselines.random_feasible: At each step choose uniformly among currently affordable actions, independent of outcomes; same Bayesian update and terminal decision
baselines.prior_only_planner: Choose EIG/cost actions using original prior every time, but still update terminal belief; planning-feedback ablation
baselines.optimal_decision_oracle: Finite-horizon dynamic program maximizing expected final MAP accuracy; explanatory upper bound, not an equally cheap learned competitor

seed_use: Freeze implementation and protocol hashes before evaluating this seed range; never relabel repeated evaluation as fresh holdout
uniform: SHA256 UTF-8 key; take first4bytes as unsigned big-endian x; u=(x+0.5)/4294967296
pairing: Same seed supplies the same hidden hypothesis and potential action/repetition outcomes to every policy; policy never receives seed or hidden state
primary: Fraction of correct final hidden-state decisions at cost2
secondary: Action frequencies and adaptive next-action changes
decision_advantage_gate: Evaluation paired accuracy advantage over best_fixed at least0.05, with approximate paired95percent interval lower endpoint above0; disclose this is a constructed synthetic benchmark
uncertainty: Paired episode difference d in{-1,0,1}; interval mean(d)+/-1.96*sample_sd(d)/sqrt(N), approximate Monte Carlo interval only
claims: Response-dependent test selection under a known finite model. No learned policy parameters, no cross-episode improvement, no self-rewriting code, no scientific discovery claim. Greedy information gain is not generally decision-optimal.
